weekday_words.rule: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" means the one in the current week; "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.

"This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.
So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
| 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |
The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`.
A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan".
`get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.
If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.
If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.

A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal.
Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.
When the attempts are used up, stop.

amounts.first_ask: Ask for the full past-due amount first; never ask how much the customer can pay; the agent proposes every amount.
amounts.too_much: Offer the floor once and say the rest stays overdue; refusing the floor is a flat refusal; attempt 2 may name the floor again on the deadline.
amounts.accept_range: Accept any amount from the floor up to the full past-due amount, both included.
amounts.below_floor: Say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once; if not accepted, it is a flat refusal.

source.quote: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
Never ask "how much can you pay?".
The agent proposes every amount.
If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Say that the rest stays overdue.
If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
Do not ask about today again for each product.
Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.
Persuasion attempts are counted per product.
If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.
Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation.
